The hourly prices of the [aWATTar HOURLY](https://www.awattar.at/tariffs/hourly)
dynamic electricity tariff, in Germany and Austria, in Gladys: the price of the current
hour, the cheapest hours of the day, a price chart for today and tomorrow, and scene
triggers to run your appliances when electricity is cheapest.

This integration is not affiliated with aWATTar or tado°. It reads the public market
data of aWATTar, tested against the live API, but it was developed without an aWATTar
contract: feedback welcome.

## Overview

aWATTar publishes, without account or key, the **hourly EPEX Spot day-ahead prices**
of Germany (DE-LU zone) and Austria (AT zone). The integration turns them into the
**aWATTar HOURLY price** of your country: not just the raw market price, but the
market price plus the aWATTar components (see _Price formula_), with or without VAT.
The raw market price of the current hour stays available on its own feature.

Tomorrow's prices are published around 14:00. Every time is shown in Central European
Time (Berlin and Vienna), and a day runs from midnight to midnight in that time,
whatever the timezone of your Gladys.

aWATTar Germany is now **tado° Energy**: the API and the tariff stay the same.

## Requirements

- Gladys Assistant 5.3.0 or later.
- Internet access from Gladys to `api.awattar.de` or `api.awattar.at`.
- Nothing else: no account, no API key, no hardware.

## Installation

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations → Install from GitHub** and enter
   `https://github.com/guim31/gladys-awattar`.
2. Open the integration, pick your country, check the tariff fields, save.
3. Open the **Discovery** tab and add the **aWATTar Deutschland** or **aWATTar
   Österreich** device.
4. On a dashboard, add the **Electricity prices** widget.

## Configuration

| Field                         | Default       | What it does                                                             |
| ----------------------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Country                       | Germany       | Market and tariff: Germany or Austria. Another country is another device |
| Include VAT                   | Yes           | Prices with the VAT rate below                                           |
| Surcharge (ct/kWh, net)       | Country value | Added to every hour before VAT. Empty: 1.5 in Austria, 0 in Germany      |
| Markup (% of market price)    | 0             | A percentage of the market price, always added as a cost. Empty: 0       |
| VAT rate (%)                  | Country value | Empty: 19 in Germany, 20 in Austria                                      |
| Language of the feature names | French        | Used when the device is added: the names do not change afterwards        |

Decimals accept a dot or a comma (`1,5`). An unreadable value falls back to the value of
the country. To see your **full price per kWh**, add your grid fees, levies and taxes
per kWh (net) to the surcharge.

The **Refresh the prices now** button reads aWATTar at once and shows what it
publishes for today and tomorrow: use it to check the connection.

## Price formula

For every hour:

`price = (market + |market| × markup % + surcharge) × (1 + VAT %)`

- **Austria**: aWATTar publishes EPEX Spot AT + 1.5 ct/kWh, plus 20 % VAT on the
  whole. aWATTar's own examples: 5.00 ct gives 7.80 ct, 0.00 ct gives 1.80 ct,
  −5.00 ct gives −4.20 ct. These are the defaults.
- **Germany**: tado° Energy publishes the EPEX Spot DE-LU price "plus further
  procurement costs, taxes, levies and grid fees", regional and not given as one
  figure. The default surcharge is 0: enter the per-kWh costs of your contract.
- Not included by default: grid fees, levies, the fixed monthly fee (Austria 5.75 €,
  Germany 4.58 € plus metering).

## The aWATTar device

One device per country, read-only, refreshed by the integration itself every minute
(the prices are read from aWATTar once an hour).

| Feature                       | Type    | Value                                                               |
| ----------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Current price (€/kWh)         | Price   | aWATTar HOURLY price of the current hour                            |
| Next hour price (€/kWh)       | Price   | Price of the next hour (after 23:00, once tomorrow is known)        |
| Average price today (€/kWh)   | Price   | Average of the hours of the day                                     |
| Lowest price today (€/kWh)    | Price   | Cheapest hour of the day                                            |
| Highest price today (€/kWh)   | Price   | Most expensive hour of the day                                      |
| Cheapest hour today           | Text    | Start of the cheapest hour, `HH:MM`                                 |
| Most expensive hour today     | Text    | Start of the most expensive hour, `HH:MM`                           |
| Hour rank (1 = cheapest)      | Counter | Rank of the current hour in the day, 1 to 24 (23 or 25 on DST days) |
| Market price now (€/kWh, net) | Price   | EPEX Spot price of the current hour, without anything added         |

Gladys has no €/kWh unit: the prices show in euros, the name says per what. When a
feature is the only one of its kind on the device, the dashboard shows the generic
label of the kind ("Counter (integer)") instead of its name.

## Dashboard widget

**Electricity prices** shows the price shown (with or without VAT), three tiles (now,
next hour, today's average), the chart of today and tomorrow with the cheapest and
the most expensive hour of each day marked and a line at the current time, then the
cheapest hour of today and tomorrow, tomorrow's average and the market price of the
current hour. Until tomorrow's prices are published, it says that they are not
published yet.

## Scene triggers

Three triggers, in the scene editor under **aWATTar**. They compare the prices of the
configuration (aWATTar HOURLY price, with or without VAT).

### Cheapest hours of the day begin

Fires once a day, at the start of the cheapest run of consecutive hours of the day.
Pick the length of the run: 1 to 6 or 8 hours (1 hour is the cheapest hour of the
day). Variables: average price of the run, start and end time.

### One of the cheapest hours begins

Fires at the start of each of the N cheapest hours of the day, consecutive or not.
Pick N: 1 to 6, 8, 10 or 12. Variables: price of the hour, its rank, start and end
time.

### The price drops below a threshold

Fires at the start of an hour whose price is below the threshold when the hour before
was not: once per cheap run. Pick the threshold: 0 ct/kWh (negative prices) to 40
ct/kWh by steps of 5. Variables: price of the hour, start time, and the end of the
cheap run as far as the known prices tell. Unlike a condition on the **Current
price** feature, it says how long the run lasts, and it works without the device.

All triggers fire when the hour begins, at most 10 minutes late (Gladys or the
integration restarting): an hour that began longer ago fires nothing.

## Scene examples

- **Dishwasher in the cheapest 3 hours**: trigger _Cheapest hours of the day begin_,
  3 hours → turn on the dishwasher plug.
- **Hot water boiler on the 4 cheapest hours**: trigger _One of the cheapest hours
  begins_, 4 → turn on the boiler; a second scene on _Hour rank_ greater than 4 →
  turn it off.
- **Negative price**: trigger _The price drops below a threshold_, 0 ct/kWh → turn on
  the boiler and send "Electricity is free until \{end_time\}".

## Refresh and API usage

aWATTar asks for fair use of its free API: 100 requests a day at most. The
integration stays well below:

- one request an hour, for today and tomorrow together;
- from 13:00, again every 15 minutes until tomorrow's prices are published, then
  hourly again (about 60 requests a day at worst);
- after a failure, retries after 5, 10, 20, 40 then 60 minutes; the last known prices
  stay in use meanwhile (prices are known a day ahead).

The states are published only when they change, plus a reminder every 6 hours.

## Troubleshooting

- **"aWATTar cannot be reached"** in the Configuration screen: Gladys has no internet
  access, or aWATTar is down. The last known prices stay in use; press **Refresh the
  prices now** to try again.
- **"publishes no price for today yet"**: aWATTar answered with no price for the day,
  a publication incident. The integration tries again every 15 minutes.
- **No value on the device**: add the device from the Discovery tab first; its values
  arrive at once.
- **Changed the country**: add the new device from the Discovery tab; the old one gets
  no more values and can be deleted.
- **Debug logs**: set `LOG_LEVEL=debug` on the container to see every refresh.

## Limitations

- Developed without an aWATTar contract: the formula follows what aWATTar publishes,
  not an invoice. Compare it with your bill and adjust the fields.
- Hourly prices, as the HOURLY tariff bills them. Should aWATTar publish quarter hours,
  they are averaged back to the hour.
- No login: no consumption, no costs, no personal prices.
- The triggers look at the current day only: a cheapest run never spans midnight.
- Read-only: nothing is controlled by the integration itself.
- The feature names are set when the device is added; changing the language later
  does not rename them.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings aWATTar asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| aWATTar HOURLY prices | `section` | No | aWATTar publishes the hourly EPEX Spot day-ahead prices of Germany and Austria, readable without an account. Tomorrow's prices arrive around 14:00. Add the aWATTar device from the Discovery tab, and the price widget from the dashboard. Developed without an aWATTar contract: feedback welcome. Not affiliated with aWATTar or tado°. |
| Country | `select` | No | The market and the tariff: Germany (EPEX Spot DE-LU, aWATTar now tado° Energy) or Austria (EPEX Spot AT). Another country is another device. |
| Include VAT | `boolean` | No | Prices with the VAT of the country (Germany 19 %, Austria 20 %), negative prices included. |
| Surcharge (ct/kWh, net) | `string` | No | Added to the market price of every hour, before VAT. Empty: aWATTar's procurement component (Austria 1.5, Germany 0). Add your grid fees and taxes per kWh to see the full price. |
| Markup (% of the market price) | `string` | No | A percentage of the market price added every hour (always a cost, negative prices too). Empty: 0, the current aWATTar HOURLY tariffs have none. |
| VAT rate (%) | `string` | No | Empty: 19 in Germany, 20 in Austria. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | No | Used when the device is added to Gladys: the names do not change afterwards. |

## How to install aWATTar in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: aWATTar appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-awattar:1.0.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-awattar](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-awattar).

aWATTar requires Gladys `>=5.3.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

aWATTar is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core.
